full_page.content:
1897, August 26
The following is a faithful transcription of the handwritten original notes by the Servant of God, Father Solanus Casey, O.F.M. Cap. (his Notebook No. 9)
FATHER SOLANUS, NOTEBOOK No. 9
Pg. 1 "You are afraid to suffer here & unwilling to go hence; what shall I do with you?" Our Lord to a sick bishop
"If I must die once, why not now?" St. Austin "Can one do better than humble that and over- come it which God has given us to master, & which a loving Providence has ordained should be humbled?" i.e. the flesh 8/98
Pg. 2 "The devil" says St. Gregory, "is a lion & a pismire both together; a lion to those who are to him but as pismires; and a pismire to such as behave themselves to him as lion." - i.e. to the courageous in temptations.
St. Paulinus of Nola from bishop - to voluntary slave etc. - a rich royal Roman (+431) - Example of Unbounded Charity - having lived in virginity with his holy wife, etc.
verichte deine leibliche Liebeswerk für den Nachsten als dientest du Christo Selber; und nehme dasselbe von Anderen an als ein Knecht.
Pg. 3 "Pray for my Inten." "Du hasst Recht! ! ! " M. Absent in N.Y. Position in choir.
"It is good not to eat flesh and not to drink wine, or anything whereby thy brother is of - fended, or scandalized, or made weak." Roman XIV 21
"My friend, I myself have renounced the world and my inheritance in orter to save my soul; do you think I could advise your son to a contrary course? Why I should think myself deserving of damnation if I did." St. Paul of the Cross to the father of St. Alfons M. de Legouri A.D. 1724
